verses.gurmukhi: ੧੮ : ਪੰਡਤ ਵੀ ਮੂਰਖ ਹੋ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ
verses.translit_en: 18 : pa(n)ddat vee moorakh ho sakadhaa hai

en.bdb: Even a pandit could be a fool

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੋਸਟਿ ਗਾਂਗੇ ਤੇਲੀਐ ਪੰਡਿਤ ਨਾਲਿ ਹੋਵੈ ਜਗੁ ਦੇਖੈ।
verses.translit_en: gosaT gaa(n)ge teleeaai pa(n)ddit naal hovai jag dhekhai|

en.bdb: A discussion between Gangu, the oilman and a pandit was being witnessed by one and all.

verses.gurmukhi: ਖੜੀ ਕਰੈ ਇਕ ਅੰਗੁਲੀ ਗਾਂਗਾ ਦੁਇ ਵੇਖਾਲੈ ਰੇਖੈ।
verses.translit_en: khaRee karai ik a(n)gulee gaa(n)gaa dhui vekhaalai rekhai|

en.bdb: Showing one finger to Gang/ the pandit indicated that the Lord is one. But Gangu thought that he wanted to extract his (Ganges) one eye and hence he showed two fingers indicating that he will bring out both of his (pandit's) eyes.

verses.gurmukhi: ਫੇਰਿ ਉਚਾਇ ਪੰਜਾਂਗੁਲਾ ਗਾਂਗਾ ਮੁਠਿ ਹਲਾਇ ਅਲੇਖੈ।
verses.translit_en: fer uchai pa(n)jaa(n)gulaa gaa(n)gaa muTh halai alekhai|

en.bdb: But the pandit thought that Gangu is hinting at the two dimensions of Lord - nirgun (beyond all virtues) and sagun, (with all virtues).

verses.gurmukhi: ਪੈਰੀ ਪੈ ਉਠਿ ਚਲਿਆ ਪੰਡਿਤੁ ਹਾਰਿ ਭੁਲਾਵੈ ਭੇਖੈ।
verses.translit_en: pairee pai uTh chaliaa pa(n)ddit haar bhulaavai bhekhai|

en.bdb: Pandit now raised five fingers to show that His two forms are due to the five elements, but, considering the pandit as indicating that with five fingers he would scratch the face of Gangu,

verses.gurmukhi: ਨਿਰਗੁਣੁ ਸਰਗੁਣੁ ਅੰਗ ਦੁਇ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਪੰਜਿ ਮਿਲਨਿ ਸਰੇਖੈ।
verses.translit_en: niragun saragun a(n)g dhui paramesar pa(n)j milan sarekhai|

en.bdb: Gangs brandished his fist showing that he would kill him by the stroke of his fist. Now pandit felt that he was being made to understand that unity of five elements was the cause of the creation.

verses.gurmukhi: ਅਖੀ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਭੰਨਸਾਂ ਮੁਕੀ ਲਾਇ ਹਲਾਇ ਨਿਮੇਖੈ।
verses.translit_en: akhee dhove(n) bha(n)nasaa(n) mukee lai halai nimekhai|

en.bdb: Mistakingly the pandit accepted his defeat and fell at his opponent's feet and left the place. In fact the fool had meant that he would bring out his eyes and attack with a tight fist but this was interpreted differently by the pandit.
Thus because of his specific thinking even the pandit was also proved a fool.
